title: Premiere's keys work on the timeline
goal: A Premiere editor reaches for the usual timeline keys (play, shuttle, in and out marks, split, ripple delete, frame step) and only the blade key works, while the arrow keys nudge a picked clip instead of stepping a frame. Make those keys do what they do in Premiere while the timeline has focus, and make the transport's buttons say what the keys really do.
notes:

from keys-copy-between-layers (2026-09-23): Video > Go to Next Key is Shift-K and Go to Previous Key is Option-K (the user's pair). When K becomes Stop for J/K/L, keep those two chords as they are; they are separate from plain K.

Adversarial review before building: (1) nearly every Premiere key collides with a Photoshop tool letter here (K lens, L line, I measure, O ellipse, A arrow, M marquee), so the timeline needs a real notion of keyboard focus. Decision: the canvas holds the keyboard by default, so a Photoshop user pressing L still gets a line; any press in the timeline dock hands the keyboard to the timeline (a thin accent ring on the dock says so), and a press on the canvas takes it back. That is Premiere's own panel-focus model. Keys with no Photoshop meaning (Space, Home, End, Cmd-K, Opt-I, Opt-O) work whichever has focus. (2) The mock's K adds a key; the task's K is Stop for J/K/L. The user's task is newer and explicit, so K is Stop on a focused timeline; Shift-K / Opt-K keep stepping keys. (3) B: Premiere's B is the Razor, the mock's B is the Blade tool, so on a document with time B picks the Blade and Cmd-K splits at the playhead (Premiere's Add Edit); the old recording window keeps B = cut. (4) The playback clock only runs at 1x forward: J/K/L needs a rate, including backwards; sound plays only at 1x forward (a shuttle at 2x/-1x is silent), which is a known gap against Premiere's pitched shuttle audio. (5) Clip pieces cannot hold a gap, so Delete (lift) on a piece shortens that clip and moves nothing else; Shift-Delete ripples. (6) A key step does not play the sound under the playhead (the open question from the scrub-audio task): Premiere's frame step is silent by default, so this matches it. (7) The DocumentTransportBar with Previous/Next Frame buttons is not reachable for a document with time any more (the dock's transport is Start / Play / End, as the mock draws); those buttons' tooltips promise Home and End, which this task binds.

Side by side with video.html (transport + .tlbar): matches the mock's Select/Blade bar and B = Blade, V = Select. Departures: the focus ring round the dock (not in the mock; Premiere's focused-panel outline, needed because one letter now means two things); a 2x/-1x readout beside the time only while shuttling; the mock's K adds a key, here K is Stop as the task asks.
